heading: Make sure the worksite reaches your team.
intro: A customer may describe work in New York or Pennsylvania using only a town name. Before replacing the website, check whether the existing inquiry gives your team enough location and job detail to respond.
customerQuestion: Can you take this job at my actual location?

decisions.label: State the coverage you actually offer
decisions.body: Describe the work and locations your team will consider. Crossing the state line should not imply a different price or eligibility rule unless your business confirms one.

decisions.label: Keep the job location in the request
decisions.body: Ask for town, state, the work needed and a useful reply route. Test distinct New York and Pennsylvania examples through both the customer acknowledgement and the message your team receives.

decisions.label: Choose the smallest useful change
decisions.body: If the details arrive correctly, clearer coverage copy may be enough. Missing details call for a focused investigation; a rebuild becomes relevant when services, navigation or retained pages also need substantial change.

ownerInputs: Your current coverage and accepted work on each side of the state line.
The existing form and an anonymized example of a request missing useful details.
A keep/change/remove list if the wider site no longer matches the business.
sourceBridge: Amber Water Pros and Junken Monkeys describe Broome and northeastern Pennsylvania coverage, making town and state useful details for this example.
limits: This is a proposed inquiry check, not a finding that either public example loses messages. A receipt does not confirm acceptance, travel or timing. Any included small repair remains conditional on safe, practical access; broader work needs an agreed scope and price.

heading: Show the order of group booking and lunch planning.
intro: Several homeschool families may be arranging one museum visit. The website can help their organizer understand the attendance roles and complete the visit booking before requesting boxed lunches.
customerQuestion: What do I need to arrange now, and what waits until our visit is booked?

decisions.label: Prepare one group request
decisions.body: Identify the intended date and aggregate attendance for the local homeschool offer. Explain the minimum group size, advance-booking requirement and one-group-per-entry-slot rule using current museum-approved terms.

decisions.label: Keep the adult roles clear
decisions.body: Distinguish the organizer from the required accompanying adults; parents count within that accompanying-adult allocation. Collect totals for the initial discussion, not children’s names or private records.

decisions.label: Add the appropriate meal step
decisions.body: Ordinary Flight Grill plans belong on the initial booking form. A boxed-lunch preorder follows a booked field trip and has its own deadline. If the date changes, review both arrangements with staff.

ownerInputs: The current group definitions, minimum attendance and booking lead time.
The approved booking and meal contacts, with their actual confirmation wording.
The separate lunch deadline and who updates instructions when a date changes.
sourceBridge: Pima Air & Space Museum’s homeschool guidance separates organizer roles, visit booking and later boxed-lunch orders, providing a concrete sequence for a group-planning page.
limits: This is a public planning example, not a museum client project. Staff decide eligibility, supervision and booking acceptance. Submitting a visit request does not book the trip or order lunches; participant records and online ordering require separate assessment.

heading: Show the conditions for each stop on a shared ticket.
intro: A ticket covering several destinations does not make their buildings interchangeable. Put each stop’s practical information beside its name so visitors can choose their outing and identify questions for staff.
customerQuestion: Which of the included places can our party plan to visit?

decisions.label: Name the destinations covered
decisions.body: List the museums or house included in the admission offer. Use the same destination names on the ticket introduction and individual building pages.

decisions.label: Keep conditions with the building
decisions.body: Give each stop its own approved pet and physical-access information. A general icon or statement should not transfer one museum’s conditions to the historic house.

decisions.label: Connect a single stop to the whole visit
decisions.body: From an individual building page, let visitors find the shared ticket and the other stops’ information. Give unresolved access questions a staff contact rather than assigning the whole party a suitable-or-unsuitable label.

ownerInputs: The current ticket inclusions and destination names.
Approved pet and physical-access wording for each building.
The responsible contact and update owner for conflicting building notices.
sourceBridge: Mohave County Historical Society describes different pet and access arrangements at its museums and Bonelli House within a shared admission offer.
limits: The public example supports a multi-building content comparison, not special expertise in every Mohave business. Do not infer the exact conditions from another building or certify an individual’s access. Staff confirm current arrangements; the website does not approve an itinerary.
